title: GameCube Controllers Connected Via the Official GCC Adapter Not Working
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.6.1, 4.7 dev 3

### System information

Arch Linux

### Issue description

Godot currently doesn't detect any inputs from GameCube controllers connected via Nintendo's official GCC Adapter.

While using the Mayflash GCC adapter in PC mode is an option that still works AFAIK, I'm interested in getting Godot to recognize controllers using the official adapter specifically, similar to Dolphin Emulator for example, or certain games like Rivals of Aether which is able to detect and use the official GCC adapter.

Alternatively, if supporting this specific device turns out to be outside the scope of Godot, any pointers on how to add support, maybe through a GDExtension, would also be appreciated. I'd be open to try implement support that way myself as well. Thanks

(also I tried to look up any existing issues about this, and found #56475, #23237, and #21550, but they all seem to be about the Mayflash adapter specifically)

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new project
2. Go to Project > Project Settings... > Input Map
3. With a GCC connected via the official adapter, attempt to add an event to an action via the event listener
